correctness.rationale: The logistic unitary gives one-sided exponential convolution without constants missing. The commutator Hilbert--Schmidt kernel identity is exact; when the positive monotone velocity tends to zero and has fixed-displacement ratio one, a dominated-convergence argument gives the precise pointwise density asymptotic 2v(s)^2. Freezing the multiplier creates trace-class approximants with rank-one norm product one, and the error has operator norm at most 4 times the tail velocity. For nonzero finite/infinite limiting velocity, translated weakly null inputs and oscillatory integration by parts rule out compactness. Power-law integration gives the 1/2 and 1 thresholds and exact coefficients. No numerical extrapolation is used as an infinite-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: The phase velocity in the logarithmic endpoint coordinate is an intrinsic, geometrically motivated parameter for unimodular oscillations. Its limiting value governs compactness, while its tail square-integrability governs Hilbert--Schmidt membership: two independent thresholds are classified. The power-chirp family gives a complete natural phase diagram and quantitative logarithmic/power energy laws at the critical ideal boundary. This identifies where unbounded endpoint oscillation can coexist with compact commutators and supplies more than finite approximation or a normalization check.
